en: The Scripture on the Four Dharmas Practiced by Bodhisattvas, as spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"You have already attained immeasurable and wholesome benefits; you should now seek the unsurpassed, great bodhi of a Buddha."
Why is this? Because the Buddha’s bodhi is equal to that which is peerless throughout both the mundane and supramundane realms.
If sentient beings of future ages resolve to seek the Buddha’s bodhi, they should cultivate four dharmas.
What are the four?
First, one should resolve to attain great bodhicitta; even at the cost of one's body and life, one must not regress.
Second, one should draw near to virtuous friends; even at the cost of one's body and life, one must not distance oneself from them.
Third, one should cultivate patience and gentleness, preferring to lose body and life rather than giving rise to anger;
fourth, one should rely on places of tranquility, preferring to lose body and life rather than thinking of clamor and distraction.
"O sons of good family!
These four dharmas are what a bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice and study.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Those who seek supreme fruition should give rise to the bodhicitta;
Exerting themselves in diligent practice, they must rely upon spiritual friends.
Patience is praised by the Buddhas, and such a person is called one of great power."
"In the empty and quiet places where the sages dwell, they are fearless like lions.
When the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he further said:

"Those who possess wisdom and great compassion, and are able to cultivate the four kinds of dharmas mentioned above, will be able to liberate themselves from birth and death, escape the net of Māra, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, and realize Great Nirvāṇa."

When the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra, those bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they received it with faith, practiced accordingly, paid their respects, and departed.
The Sūtra on the Four Dharmas Practiced by Bodhisattvas Spoken by the Buddha
